questions.question: Q: Describe the lifecycle of a star like the Sun.
questions.correctAnswer: Nebula → protostar → main sequence (hydrogen fusion) → red giant (helium fusion) → planetary nebula → white dwarf.

questions.question: Q: What happens to a star more than 8 times the mass of the Sun?
questions.correctAnswer: It becomes a red supergiant, undergoes further fusion stages up to iron, then explodes as a supernova. The core becomes a neutron star (if <3 M☉) or a black hole (if >3 M☉).

questions.question: Q: What is the Chandrasekhar limit?
questions.correctAnswer: ~1.4 solar masses — the maximum mass a white dwarf can have. Above this, electron degeneracy pressure cannot support it and it collapses further.

questions.question: Q: Why does a main-sequence star remain stable?
questions.correctAnswer: Hydrostatic equilibrium: gravitational collapse is balanced by outward radiation pressure from nuclear fusion.

questions.question: Q: What is a planetary nebula?
questions.correctAnswer: The ejected outer layers of a low-mass star at the end of its life, forming an expanding shell of gas illuminated by the hot exposed core.
